intro.title: Write request deduplication for identical fetches
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a request deduplication function to prevent sending multiple identical network requests at the same time. You will learn how to use a Map object to track ongoing requests by their unique identifiers, such as URLs. The core programming concept involves caching promises to ensure that duplicate requests reuse the same pending promise instead of creating new ones. You will work with JavaScript's fetch API, async/await, and promise handling. By the end, you'll have a reusable utility that improves application performance by reducing unnecessary network traffic.
intro.usecase: Request deduplication is a critical performance pattern in modern web applications, especially in data-rich dashboards and interactive UIs. For example, in a financial dashboard where multiple widgets might simultaneously request the same stock price data, deduplication prevents redundant network calls, reducing server load and speeding up the interface. Similarly, in an e-commerce product page with multiple recommendation panels, deduplicating identical product detail fetches ensures a smoother user experience and conserves bandwidth. This pattern is essential for developers building efficient, scalable frontends that handle concurrent data fetching without waste.
